MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a multiple of 3? (1 mark)
   A. 50
   B. 51
   C. 53
   D. 52

2. Which is the smallest number: 819, 891, 189, 918? (1 mark)
   A. 891
   B. 189
   C. 918
   D. 819

3. What number is the Roman numeral VII? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 3
   C. 2
   D. 1

4. What is the smallest 5-digit number? (1 mark)
   A. 9,999
   B. 10,000
   C. 99,999
   D. 1,000

5. A farmer picked 1,275 mangoes on Monday and 3,548 mangoes on Tuesday. How many mangoes did he pick? (1 mark)
   A. 4,713 mangoes
   B. 4,923 mangoes
   C. 4,823 mangoes
   D. 4,813 mangoes

6. A stadium seats 9,000 people. If 6,450 seats are taken, how many seats are empty? (1 mark)
   A. 2,550 seats
   B. 2,540 seats
   C. 2,650 seats
   D. 3,450 seats

7. Estimate 7,483 − 2,196 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 5,270
   B. 5,280
   C. 5,380
   D. 5,290

8. What is 12 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 112
   B. 1,200
   C. 120
   D. 12,000

9. Work out 12 × 21. (1 mark)
   A. 262
   B. 36
   C. 242
   D. 252

10. Work out 19 × 31. (1 mark)
   A. 599
   B. 589
   C. 579
   D. 76

11. Chebet writes some more fractions. Which of these is an improper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 5/12
   B. 7/10
   C. 9/9
   D. 2 5/8

12. Change 6 2/3 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 20/3
   B. 8/3
   C. 18/3
   D. 21/3

13. In the number 13.42, the digit 4 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Ones
   B. Tenths
   C. Tens
   D. Hundredths

14. Otieno is a years old. His sister is 3 years older. Which expression shows his sister's age? (1 mark)
   A. a − 3
   B. a + 3
   C. 3a
   D. a ÷ 3

15. Change 1,200 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 12 m
   B. 13 m
   C. 1 m 20 cm
   D. 12 m 50 cm

16. An L-shaped garden has sides of 6 m, 2 m, 3 m, 2 m, 3 m and 4 m. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 19 m
   B. 20 m
   C. 18 m
   D. 24 m

17. What does area measure? (1 mark)
   A. How long a line is
   B. How much flat surface a shape covers
   C. How heavy an object is
   D. How much water a container holds

18. A rectangle has an area of 72 square units and 9 rows. How many columns does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 81
   B. 9
   C. 63
   D. 8

19. Cuboid A is 6 by 2 by 2 blocks (length, width, height). Cuboid B is 3 by 3 by 3 blocks. Which has the greater volume? (1 mark)
   A. Cuboid A
   B. It cannot be told
   C. They are equal
   D. Cuboid B

20. A bucket holds 10 L. A boy pours 3 cans of 2 L into it. How many more litres are needed to fill it? (1 mark)
   A. 7 L
   B. 4 L
   C. 1 L
   D. 6 L

21. A big sponge is light but a small stone is heavy. What does this tell us? (1 mark)
   A. Small things are always light
   B. Mass is measured in metres
   C. Big things are always heavy
   D. Size does not tell us the mass

22. What is 1 3/4 kg + 2 1/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 4 kg
   B. 4 1/2 kg
   C. 3 3/4 kg
   D. 4 1/4 kg

23. How many days are in 5 weeks? (1 mark)
   A. 25 days
   B. 35 days
   C. 42 days
   D. 120 days

24. Lunch is at one o'clock in the afternoon. How do we write this time? (1 mark)
   A. 1:00 p.m.
   B. 1:00 noon
   C. 12:00 p.m. and 1:00 a.m.
   D. 1:00 a.m.

25. What is 4 h 35 min + 3 h 40 min? (1 mark)
   A. 8 h 5 min
   B. 8 h 15 min
   C. 7 h 15 min
   D. 8 h 25 min

26. How many days are in 6 weeks? (1 mark)
   A. 30 days
   B. 49 days
   C. 42 days
   D. 144 days

27. 700 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 0.70
   B. Ksh 7
   C. Ksh 8
   D. Ksh 70

28. Two half turns together make (1 mark)
   A. a full turn
   B. a quarter turn
   C. a half turn
   D. two full turns

29. Which fold gives a line of symmetry of a rectangle that is not a square? (1 mark)
   A. Along a diagonal
   B. Across the middle from side to side
   C. Along one of the short sides
   D. From one corner to the middle of the opposite long side

30. In a tally chart, 4 more single tally marks are drawn. What number do they show? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 9
   C. 3
   D. 4

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write instructions for a person to walk from the classroom door to the school gate using at least two turns. Use words such as forward, quarter turn, clockwise and anticlockwise. (4 marks)

32. A hall floor is covered with 12 rows of 15 square tiles. (a) How many tiles cover the floor? (b) A smaller room has 9 rows of 12 tiles. How many more tiles does the hall need than the smaller room? (5 marks)

33. Using each of the digits 4, 0, 7 and 2 once, write the largest and the smallest 4-digit numbers you can make. (4 marks)

34. A rectangular field is 45 m long and 30 m wide. (a) Find its perimeter. (b) A farmer wants to fence it but leaves two gates of 3 m each. How many metres of fence does he need? (5 marks)

35. A signboard has four straight sides. Two sides are 50 cm and two are 30 cm. All four corners are square. Name the shape and give a reason. (3 marks)

36. How can you tell that a cuboid is a cube? Give one example of each from everyday life. (3 marks)

37. Write 5x + 3y − 2x + y in its simplest form. (3 marks)

38. Share 96 metres of rope equally into pieces of 8 metres. How many pieces are there? (2 marks)

39. In the number 27,150, give the place value and the total value of the digit 7. (4 marks)

40. Estimate 5,382 + 3,617 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. Then find the exact sum. (4 marks)

41. Cuboid A is 10 by 2 by 2 blocks and cuboid B is 5 by 4 by 3 blocks. Work out both volumes and say which is greater. (4 marks)

42. Estimate 38 × 22 by rounding to the nearest ten. Then find the exact product. (4 marks)

43. Write 7,206 in expanded form. (2 marks)

44. Explain how you can use addition to check a subtraction. Use 7,865 − 3,542 = 4,323 as an example. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — 51
   51 = 3 × 17, so 51 is a multiple of 3.

2. B — 189
   Compare the digits from the left. The smallest number is 189.

3. A — 7
   VII stands for 7.

4. B — 10,000
   Adding 1 to 9,999 gives 10,000, the smallest number with five digits.

5. C — 4,823 mangoes
   Add 1,275 + 3,548 = 4,823 mangoes.

6. A — 2,550 seats
   Subtract 9,000 − 6,450 = 2,550. Check by adding: 2,550 + 6,450 = 9,000.

7. B — 5,280
   7,483 rounds to 7,480 and 2,196 rounds to 2,200. 7,480 − 2,200 = 5,280.

8. B — 1,200
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 12 × 100 = 1,200.

9. D — 252
   12 × 1 = 12 and 12 × 20 = 240. 12 + 240 = 252.

10. B — 589
   19 × 1 = 19 and 19 × 30 = 570. 19 + 570 = 589.

11. C — 9/9
   In an improper fraction the numerator is equal to or bigger than the denominator. 9/9 is one whole or more.

12. A — 20/3
   6 × 3 = 18 and 18 + 2 = 20. The denominator stays 3, so the answer is 20/3.

13. B — Tenths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 13.42 the digit 4 is in the tenths place.

14. B — a + 3
   Older means add, so her age is a + 3.

15. A — 12 m
   1,200 ÷ 100 = 12 remainder 0. So 1,200 cm = 12 m.

16. B — 20 m
   Add every side: 6 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 20 m.

17. B — How much flat surface a shape covers
   Area is the amount of flat surface covered by a shape.

18. D — 8
   Rows × columns = 72, so columns = 72 ÷ 9 = 8.

19. D — Cuboid B
   A = 6 × 2 × 2 = 24 blocks. B = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 blocks. Cuboid B is greater.

20. B — 4 L
   3 × 2 = 6 L poured in. 10 − 6 = 4 L more.

21. D — Size does not tell us the mass
   We must measure to know the mass. Size alone does not tell us.

22. A — 4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 1 3/4 kg + 2 1/4 kg = 4 kg.

23. B — 35 days
   1 week = 7 days, so 5 × 7 = 35 days.

24. A — 1:00 p.m.
   Times from midnight to noon use a.m. and times from noon to midnight use p.m. The correct answer is 1:00 p.m..

25. B — 8 h 15 min
   Add the minutes and hours, then change 60 minutes into 1 hour. The answer is 8 h 15 min.

26. C — 42 days
   1 week = 7 days, so 6 × 7 = 42 days.

27. B — Ksh 7
   700 ÷ 100 = 7 remainder 0, so it is Ksh 7.

28. A — a full turn
   Two halves make one whole turn.

29. B — Across the middle from side to side
   Folding across the middle makes the two halves match exactly. A diagonal does not, because the corners do not fit on each other.

30. D — 4
   0 × 5 + 4 = 4.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: Walk forward 10 steps. Make a quarter turn clockwise. Walk forward 5 steps. Make a quarter turn anticlockwise. Walk to the gate.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the first move with steps, 1 mark for a turn with its size, 1 mark for the turn direction, 1 mark for clear order.

32. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 180 tiles (b) 72 more tiles
   Working / marking points: (a) 12 × 15: 12 × 10 = 120 and 12 × 5 = 60, so 180 (2 marks); smaller room 9 × 12 = 108 (1 mark); 180 − 108 (1 mark); 72 tiles (1 mark).

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Largest: 7,420. Smallest: 2,047.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for 7,420 (digits in descending order). 2 marks for 2,047 (a 4-digit number cannot begin with 0).

34. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 150 m (b) 144 m
   Working / marking points: (a) 45 + 30 + 45 + 30 = 150 m (2 marks for method, 1 mark for the answer with unit); (b) 2 × 3 = 6 m and 150 − 6 = 144 m (2 marks total, awarded 1 for 6 m and 1 for 144 m). Total 5 marks.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: A rectangle, because opposite sides are equal but not all sides are equal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the name, 1 mark for opposite sides equal, 1 mark for not all sides equal.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: In a cube the length, width and height are equal. Example of a cube: a dice. Example of a cuboid that is not a cube: a matchbox or a brick.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the property, 1 mark for each example.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3x + 4y
   Working / marking points: x terms: 5x − 2x = 3x (1 mark). y terms: 3y + y = 4y (1 mark). Answer 3x + 4y (1 mark).

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: 12 pieces
   Working / marking points: 96 ÷ 8 = 12. 1 mark for the division and 1 mark for the answer.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Place value: thousands. Total value: 7 × 1,000 = 7,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for thousands; 1 mark for 7 × 1,000; 1 mark for the answer 7,000; 1 mark for clear working.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 5,380 + 3,620 = 9,000. Exact: 8,999.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rounded number, 1 mark for the estimate 9,000, 1 mark for the exact sum 8,999.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: A = 40 blocks, B = 60 blocks. B is greater by 20 blocks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for the volumes, 1 mark for the comparison, 1 mark for the difference.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 40 × 20 = 800. Exact: 836.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding to 40 and 20, 1 mark for 800, 1 mark for 38 × 2 = 76 and 38 × 20 = 760, 1 mark for 836.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: 7,000 + 200 + 6
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 7,000 and 200; 1 mark for 6 ones with no tens.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Add the answer to the number that was taken away: 4,323 + 3,542 = 7,865, which is the starting number, so the subtraction is correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying add the answer and the smaller number, 1 mark for the example, 1 mark for saying the result matches the starting number.
